entity_reviews.extracted_value: description=Cold pressing to form sheet-type composite cathode

entity_reviews.llm_reasoning: The paper explicitly describes fabrication steps involving pressing: it states good interfacial contact can be achieved by "cold pressing" and also mentions "pressing at 430 MPa" for the composite cathode with the ionomer (Page 5). This supports that a synthesis/fabrication operation includes pressing.

The paper text explicitly states: “the FT-IR spectrum of the PTFE-based ionomer shows new peaks at 970 and 1060 cm−1” (Page 2), matching the extracted peak positions (970 cm−1 and 1060 cm−1). Alleged provenance Figure S1b is consistent with the statement referencing Figure S1b for the ionomer FT-IR spectrum.

Two of the three conductivity entries are explicitly stated in the paper text: Li6PS5Cl = 4.1 mS cm−1 and Li6PS5Cl–PTFE composite = 2.9 mS cm−1 (“The ionic conductivity of Li6PS5Cl, 4.1 mS cm−1, exceeds that of the Li6PS5Cl−PTFE composite, 2.9 mS cm−1 …”). The third entry is also stated, but the compound is mislabeled: the text reports “The ionic conductivity of the ionomer in the fully dry state was measured to be 1.6 × 10−5 S cm−1 at 25 °C.” The extracted value lists this as ‘dry ionomer’ (reasonable), but the field says ‘compound’: ‘dry ionomer’ rather than ‘ionomer’/‘PTFE-based ionomer’. Also, the alleged provenance ‘Figure S1c’ is incorrect for the conductivity measurement context in the main text (conductivities were determined by AC impedance spectroscopy in Figure S2; Figure S1c is referenced only parenthetically for the PTFE comparison). Because the extracted list includes an incorrect compound label for the third item and provenance mismatch, the extraction as given is not fully correct.
entity_reviews.llm_suggested_fix: Update the third record compound to ‘ionomer (fully dry state)’ or ‘PTFE-based ionomer (fully dry state)’ with value 1.6×10−5 S cm−1 at 25 °C. Provenance: main text (page 2) and conductivity measurement figure noted as Figure S2 (with PTFE comparison referencing Figure S1c).

This directly supports the two extracted chemical shifts (2.5 ppm and −0.2 ppm).

The paper explicitly states: “The cyclic voltammograms of the Li6PS5Cl–binder composites (Figure S5) confirm that both PTFE and the ionomer are electrochemically stable up to 3.9 V vs Li–In (4.5 V vs Li/Li+).” This directly supports an electrochemical stability window/limit of 3.9 V vs Li–In referenced to Figure S5.

The text explicitly states: “A cross-sectional SEM image of a composite cathode prepared with the ionomer (Figure S8a) shows good interfacial contact between the NCM particles, solid electrolyte, and conducting carbon.” This directly supports the extracted metric ‘interfacial contact quality’ with value ‘good’ for SEM (cross-section), and matches the alleged provenance (Figure S8a).

The text explicitly states: “A TOF-SIMS image mapping the SO3− groups of a composite cathode prepared with the ionomer (Figure S9) confirms its homogeneous distribution.” This directly supports the extracted metric (SO3− distribution) and value (homogeneous), with provenance Figure S9.
